title: Incorrect birthday for Rep. Russ Fulcher (F000469): 1973-07-19 should be 1962-03-09 (or 1963-03-09)
body:
Rep. Russ Fulcher's `bio.birthday` in `legislators-current.yaml` is recorded as `1973-07-19`. Multiple independent sources — including the two reference sites this dataset itself links for him via its `wikipedia` and `wikidata` ids — give a birth date of **March 9, 1962** (Wikipedia) or **March 9, 1963** (Wikidata), and his documented career timeline is impossible for a 1973 birth. The recorded value appears to be off by a decade, with the wrong month and day as well.

## Current data (verified 2026-07-10, `main` branch)

```yaml
- id:
    bioguide: F000469
    fec:
    - H8ID01124
    govtrack: 412773
    wikipedia: Russ Fulcher
    wikidata: Q7381134
    ...
  name:
    first: Russ
    last: Fulcher
    official_full: Russ Fulcher
  bio:
    gender: M
    birthday: '1973-07-19'
```

## Evidence the date is wrong

**1. Wikipedia** (the article this record's own `wikipedia: Russ Fulcher` id points to) opens with:

> "Russell Mark Fulcher (born **March 9, 1962**) is an American businessman and politician serving as the U.S. representative for Idaho's 1st congressional district since 2019."

The infobox uses `{{birth date and age|1962|3|9}}`.

**2. Wikidata** (the entity this record's own `wikidata: Q7381134` id points to) has P569 (date of birth) = **1963-03-09** (day precision, normal rank).

Note Wikipedia and Wikidata disagree with each other on the year (1962 vs 1963) — that one-year discrepancy may be worth resolving while fixing this — but both agree on **March 9** and both contradict `1973-07-19` by a full decade.

**3. Career timeline is impossible for a 1973 birth** (all facts from the linked Wikipedia article):

| Fact | Age if born 1973-07-19 |
|---|---|
| BBA, Boise State University, **1984** | **11** |
| MBA, Boise State University, **1988** | **15** |
| Idaho Senate member from **2005** (served to 2014) | 31 (possible, but see above) |
| Idaho Senate Majority Caucus Leader from **2008** | 34 |

A bachelor's degree earned at age 11 rules the recorded date out on the dataset's own cross-referenced sources.

## Provenance

The incorrect value is not a recent regression: it was already `birthday: '1973-07-19'` when Fulcher was first added to `legislators-current.yaml` for the 116th Congress (present in commit `49929bde58a590a564fa67ac262011ce88f98074`, ca. 2019-01-10), and it persists unchanged in current `main`. So it has been propagating to downstream consumers for the entirety of his House service.

## How we noticed

We consume this dataset in an entity-resolution pipeline that cross-checks member attributes against other sources. Fulcher's record was the only one in our current-members set whose birth year conflicted with Wikidata/Wikipedia by more than a year, which flagged it for manual review.

## Suggested fix

```yaml
  bio:
    gender: M
    birthday: '1962-03-09'
```

`1962-03-09` matches Wikipedia (and the most common value in press coverage); if the maintainers' preferred primary source (e.g., CQ/Almanac) says 1963, `1963-03-09` would match Wikidata. Either way the month/day should be March 9 and the year should be 1962 or 1963, not 1973.

Happy to submit a PR if that's preferred.

title: Facebook handle RogerMarshallMD assigned to both M001198 and T000278
body:
`legislators-social-media.yaml` gives the same Facebook handle to two senators:

- line 2550 — `bioguide: M001198` (Roger Marshall, R-KS) → `facebook: RogerMarshallMD`
- line 3263 — `bioguide: T000278` (Tommy Tuberville, R-AL) → `facebook: RogerMarshallMD`

It's the only Facebook handle shared by two members in the file (checked against the published `legislators-social-media.json`, current `main`).

M001198 looks correct: marshall.senate.gov links facebook.com/RogerMarshallMD.

T000278 looks wrong. tuberville.senate.gov links **facebook.com/SenatorTuberville**, which is the official account and resolves fine. That page also carries a stray `http://www.facebook.com/RogerMarshallMD` link alongside it, which may be where the mis-assignment came from.

Suggested fix:

```yaml
- id:
    bioguide: T000278
    govtrack: 456796
  social:
    twitter: SenTuberville
    twitter_id: 1345739193721487362
    facebook: SenatorTuberville
```

Happy to open a PR if that's the preferred route.

title: Fix Tuberville's Facebook handle (T000278)
body:
Fixes #1059.

`T000278` (Tommy Tuberville) carried `facebook: RogerMarshallMD`, which is `M001198`'s (Roger Marshall) account — the only Facebook handle claimed by two members in the file.

**Evidence for the replacement.** tuberville.senate.gov links two different Facebook URLs:

- `https://www.facebook.com/SenatorTuberville/` — the visible Facebook icon in the site's social row, i.e. the account the office presents as its own.
- `http://www.facebook.com/RogerMarshallMD` — appears only in the page's Yoast SEO metadata, as `<meta property="article:publisher">` and in the JSON-LD `sameAs` array.

The second looks like a copy-paste leftover in the site's SEO plugin configuration, and since `article:publisher` is the field a scraper would naturally read, it's a plausible origin for the mis-assignment.

M001198's own entry is unchanged: marshall.senate.gov links facebook.com/RogerMarshallMD, so that handle is correctly his.

Verified after the edit: the file still parses, all 518 records intact, and no Facebook handle is shared by two members.

title: Rep. Wahab sworn in, and fix party on Rep. Blair
Senate Finance jurisdiction_source points at the Ethics Committee's jurisdiction page
body:
`committees-current.yaml` gives the Senate Committee on Finance the Ethics Committee's `jurisdiction_source`.

```yaml
- type: senate
  name: Senate Committee on Finance
  url: http://www.finance.senate.gov/
  thomas_id: SSFI
  jurisdiction_source: https://www.ethics.senate.gov/public/index.cfm/jurisdiction
```

The `jurisdiction` text on that entry is correct and is Finance's own ("legislative jurisdiction on matters relating to taxation, debt, customs, foreign trade, and health programs under the Social Security Act..."). Only the citation is wrong, which is the awkward case for anyone quoting the field: following it lands the reader on a real page about a different committee.

Suggested fix, verified returning 200 on 2026-09-11 and carrying Finance's own jurisdiction text:

```yaml
  jurisdiction_source: https://www.finance.senate.gov/about/jurisdiction
```

Checking the whole file the same way, by comparing the host of `jurisdiction_source` against the host of `url`, this is the only entry where the source points at a different committee. One other entry differs but in the opposite direction: House Committee on Education and Workforce has `url: http://edlabor.house.gov/`, the name the committee used before it was renamed, while its `jurisdiction_source` is on the current `edworkforce.house.gov`. That looks like a stale `url` rather than a wrong source.

Happy to send a PR for either or both if that is easier than patching it directly.

title: committee_membership.py: Sen. Graham Nordone is dropped from all 17 of her committee assignments
body:
Sen. Darline Graham Nordone (SC, `G000608`) does not appear anywhere in
`committee-membership-current.yaml`, though senate.gov lists her on 17 committees and
subcommittees. She was sworn in 2026-07-14; `committee_membership.py` has run at least
twice since (2026-07-15, 2026-09-02) and has silently dropped her each time.

### Cause

`scrape_senate_member` looks senators up by `(state, last_name)`, where `last_name` comes from
`legislators-current.yaml` → `name.last`. Hers is **`Graham Nordone`**:

```yaml
- id:
    bioguide: G000608
  name:
    first: Darline
    last: Graham Nordone
    official_full: Darline Graham
```

senate.gov's committee XML gives the shorter form:

```xml
<member><name><first>Darline</first><last>Graham</last></name><state>SC</state><party>R</party><position>Member</position></member>
```

So the lookup is `("SC", "Graham")`, which misses, and the member is dropped:

```python
if (state, last_name) not in senators:
  print("\t[%s] Unknown member: %s" % (state, last_name))
  return None
```

The `print` goes to stdout mid-run, so it is easy to miss in the output of a full scrape.

### Fix

One line, in the same form as the existing `Luján` alias directly above it.

### Scope

I checked every current Senate committee XML (21 committees, including all subcommittee
blocks) against the `senators` dict built from `legislators-current.yaml`. She is the **only**
unmatched member — no other senator is affected today.

These are the 17 seats currently missing, all `position` = Member:

| thomas_id | committee |

The underlying mismatch is that senate.gov uses a shorter surname than `name.last` for members
with compound surnames. A fallback — on miss, retry against `official_full` built from the
XML's `first` + `last` — would catch this class without a per-member alias. Her `official_full`
is exactly `Darline Graham`, so it resolves cleanly. I kept this PR to the one-line alias
because it matches what the file already does and carries no risk to existing matches, but I am
glad to write the general version if you prefer it.

title: Correct House service dates for the 101st–107th Congresses
body:
Correct House service boundaries in the 101st–107th Congresses to follow the README: start is the known swearing-in day; end is the last day served. Several starts currently use election dates or an incorrect year, while several ends continue beyond death or resignation.

This changes 52 term-date values and Robinson’s dependent final affiliation end in the current/historical YAML. Identities, names, term lists and other values remain unchanged. It adds no missing terms and leaves unresolved anomalies outside this patch. The commits separate the original corrections, additional same-class corrections, two one-day resignations and the remaining special-election oath dates.

The primary evidence below distinguishes election dates from oath dates. Biographies supply election/service context; they do not corroborate every corrected oath date. The Congressional Record supplies the contemporary oath/effective-date evidence, while House history supplies official historical end dates. These institutional sources are not treated as independent publisher votes.

Three source discrepancies are explicit: Fuster’s Directory footnote says March 3, but his resignation letter makes it effective March 4; Wilson’s Directory footnote says October 9, but his letter says the expiration of October 8; Brady’s House vacancies page says March 21 before his May 19 election, while the Record oath and Directory agree on May 21.

Validation: all four CircleCI commands pass (`python test/workout.py`, `pyflakes .`, `python test/are_files_linted.py`, `python test/validate.py`). Recursive source and generated-JSON comparisons contain exactly the 53 approved date leaves, with no other parsed changes. The validator still prints pre-existing district-office diagnostics that it deliberately excludes from its exit result; this is not a clean-diagnostics claim. body:
Updates `legislators-social-media.yaml` for 82 House members, using each member's own official .house.gov home page as the source.

**How it was checked**
- Each value is the account the member's official .house.gov home page links. The pages were read on 2026-11-01, and each fix is still confirmed by a daily automated check of the same pages through 2026-11-07.
- Party and caucus accounts linked in page footers (for example House Democrats, @HouseGOP) were left out. So was one page that links another member's account.
- **YouTube:** `youtube_id` is the channel the member's page links, read from that channel's own page. Where an existing `youtube` name belongs to a different channel, it is removed.
- **Changed handles:** where a `twitter` or `instagram` handle changed, the old `twitter_id` / `instagram_id` is removed, because it belonged to the old handle. Your scripts can fill them in again.
- 15 members had no entry yet. These are new members of the 119th Congress, plus a few earlier gaps.

title: Sen. Moody / Sen. Husted updates
body:
Their term end dates have past but they are still serving:

* Sen. Moody wins special election to complete the term. Unclear if there's a swearing in date that should be represented here.
* Extend Sen. Husted's term to the expected end date. He lost special election but the expected term date was too soon. See https://ohiocapitaljournal.com/2026/11/13/ohios-u-s-senator-elect-sherrod-brown-could-get-an-early-start-in-washington/.

title: husted and moody have incorrect term info
body: both senators terms are listed as ended on november 03, 2026, but they both really end on January 3, 2029
